exposure: Maternal COVID-19 infection before 8 weeks of pregnancy
outcome: Complications during pregnancy (diabetes mellitus, preeclampsia, thyroid abnormalities)
cohort: The study included two groups: mothers infected with COVID-19 during pregnancy and a control group, along with their newborn outcomes.
finding: Maternal COVID-19 infection during pregnancy was associated with a significantly higher prevalence of cardiac ultrasound abnormalities in newborns, particularly when infection occurred before 8 weeks of gestation, and there was an observed increase in the annual incidence rates of CHD during the COVID-19 pandemic.
mod_finding: No significant differences were found in the rate of cesarean delivery between the COVID-19 cases and the control group.
birth_weight: N/A (birth weight was measured but no specific values or ranges for inclusion were stated, only that no significant differences were found between groups)
